A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 32 pages of v2 and 31 pages of v3, including figures, equations, and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic NPIV experiments and spectral-alignment analyses, including dSprites results in Appendix D.2 and Figure 6.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and analyses in Section 6 and Appendices E–F, including the dSprites results in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The contrastive feature-learning objective, neural architecture, regularization, and downstream 2SLS procedure are retained. The diagnostic procedure highlighted in v3 Section 5 already appeared in v2 Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same controlled one-dimensional NPIV scenarios and dSprites benchmark. V3 Section 6.2 expands the presentation of coverage already present in v2 Appendix D.2.

E2.justification: The oracle-feature versus learned-feature 2SLS comparison is retained. Newly discussed Fast IV is not evaluated, and v3 attributes the cited dSprites performance comparisons to Sun et al.

E3.justification: The 100,000 feature-learning samples, separate 10,000 regression samples, 50 learned features, MSE evaluation, and synthetic controls are retained. V3 newly documents the existing dSprites construction without establishing a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Spectral-decay and alignment sensitivity, partial-support cases, learned-density comparisons, and diagnostic-reliability analyses are retained. V2 Appendices C–D correspond to v3 Appendices E–F.

E5.justification: Both versions report 500 repetitions per Figure 1 parameter setting, the same bootstrap-based pseudo-confidence sets, and confidence intervals from nine independently trained dSprites models.

E6.justification: All six existing result figures retain identical image content and corresponding findings. Both versions report that approximately 85% of the dSprites structural function's squared norm is captured by the leading 10 functions, with support typically captured by 32 features.

T1.justification: New Appendix B specializes the retained Corollary 1 using polynomial singular-value decay and a source condition, deriving an explicit convergence rate and dimension choice with a cited tightness claim. Appendix F also corrects an alignment-bound projection from u-space to v-space. The main theorems and their proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list now explicitly claim a practical spectral-diagnostic procedure and its dSprites application. These were already documented in v2 Appendix D, while the central generalization-bound and good–bad–ugly claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 corrects the description of larger c_alpha values from stronger to weaker alignment. Appendix B adds interpretations connecting source regularity, spectral decay, and feature-learning error, although its claim that larger p slows convergence conflicts with its displayed rate at fixed r. Section 6.2 also adds a qualification about dSprites identifiability.

D1.justification: Section 6.2 newly specifies the dSprites image dimensions, instrument components, outcome construction, structural function, and deterministic image weights. V2's appendix gave substantially less setup information. These are additional disclosures for the retained experiment.

R1.justification: V3 adds references on rate optimality, dSprites, Fast IV, and deep proxy learning. Appendix D adds a substantive comparison distinguishing Fast IV's learned instrument kernel from paired spectral features. The central positioning relative to Sun et al. remains.

P1.justification: V3 foregrounds existing appendix material through Sections 5 and 6.2, adds background and learning-rate appendices before the retained proofs, and revises transitions and acknowledgements. Most existing prose and the main theoretical sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: V3 reformats the document throughout in NeurIPS style, changing the title and author block, typography, text width, spacing, and figure sizing and placement. It adds an illustrative dSprites image as Figure 3; the six existing scientific figures retain their graphics.

improvement.justification: V3 improves access to the existing diagnostic contribution and supplies useful dSprites construction details. However, new Appendix B says larger p slows convergence, while its displayed rate n^(-r/[2(r+1)+1/p]) becomes faster with increasing p at fixed r. With the empirical evidence and main theorems otherwise retained, the documentation gains and this introduced theoretical inconsistency leave the net quality direction uncertain.
